Near is a privacy-awareness app that helps you stay informed about your surroundings in an era of discreet Wearable cameras.

As Smart Glasses capable of recording video, audio, and spatial data become more popular devices like Ray-Ban Meta, Apple Vision Pro, Snapchat Spectacles and others, Near gives you a technical tool to detect them. It works by reading the wireless advertising signals that every Smart Glasses passively broadcasts, identifying them by their manufacturer signatures, and alerting you when a known device gets too close.

Features
Modern radar visualisation for nearby devices
Fast and responsive scanning
Background Radar Mode for continuous discovery*
Device history to revisit previously detected devices
Clear signal strength indicators to estimate proximity
Privacy-first design your data stays on your device

Nearby is built around one simple philosophy: powerful tools should feel effortless. Instead of overwhelming you with technical information, it presents what matters in a clean, thoughtful experience.

*Background scanning availability may vary depending on iOS system limitations and permissions.

description:
Weet wanneer camerabrillen bij je in de buurt zijn.

Slimme brillen zoals Ray-Ban Meta zien eruit als gewone brillen, maar kunnen je zonder geluid filmen. Mensen zijn gefilmd in cafés, in de trein en op school, en kwamen daar pas achter toen de video online stond. Glasshole Radar luistert naar het Bluetooth-signaal dat deze brillen uitzenden en laat je weten wanneer ze dichtbij zijn.

Gratis. Geen account. Je detecties blijven op je iPhone.

HOE HET HELPT
• Live radar: zie in één oogopslag of er camerabrillen in de buurt zijn, en hoe dichtbij: Heel dichtbij, In de buurt of Binnen bereik.
• Meldingen: krijg een melding wanneer er brillen verschijnen, en bekijk de radar op het toegangsscherm en in de Dynamic Island.
• Wat je kunt doen: duidelijke vervolgstappen voor dat moment, van afstand nemen tot personeel aanspreken.
• Nieuws: artikelen met bronnen over waarom camerabrillen mensen zorgen baren, met een link naar elk origineel artikel.
• Geschiedenis: wanneer brillen zijn gezien en hoe dichtbij ze kwamen, alleen bewaard op je iPhone.

WAAR HET NAAR ZOEKT
• Ray-Ban Meta- en Oakley Meta-brillen
• Snap Spectacles
• Diverse andere Bluetooth-camerabrillen

WEES DUIDELIJK OVER DE BEPERKINGEN
• Radar kan alleen brillen zien die zijn ingeschakeld en een Bluetooth-signaal uitzenden. Sommige brillen doen dat alleen op bepaalde momenten, bijvoorbeeld wanneer ze worden ingeschakeld of uit de case worden gehaald. Daardoor kan Radar brillen missen die al in gebruik zijn.
• Radar kan niet zien of de bril opneemt.
• Andere apparaten van dezelfde bedrijven kunnen soms ook een match veroorzaken.
• Meldingen op de achtergrond zijn op basis van best effort. iOS bepaalt hoe vaak apps mogen scannen wanneer het scherm uit staat.

PRIVACY
Je detecties en geschiedenis verlaten je iPhone nooit. Als je toestemming geeft, stuurt de app anonieme aantallen van welke functies worden gebruikt, zonder locatie, apparaatnamen of persoonlijke gegevens. Je kunt dit uitschakelen in Instellingen.

Glasses Radar detects nearby smart glasses by recognizing their Bluetooth advertisement signatures in real time.

When someone wearing Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, Snap Spectacles, or other camera-equipped smart eyewear is within range, Glasses Radar picks up the unique Bluetooth patterns their glasses broadcast and alerts you.

HOW IT WORKS
Smart glasses constantly broadcast Bluetooth Low Energy signals while worn. Glasses Radar reads these advertisement packets and matches them against a database of known device signatures — not just manufacturer IDs, but full byte-level fingerprints. This means fewer false alarms from other Meta devices like earbuds or Quest headsets.

WHAT IT DETECTS
- Ray-Ban Meta (all generations)
- Oakley Meta
- Snap Spectacles
- Other BLE-broadcasting smart eyewear

PRIVACY FIRST
- Entirely on-device — no account, no cloud, no data uploaded
- Zero personal data collected or stored
- Works without an internet connection

HONEST ABOUT LIMITS
Detection is probabilistic. A result means glasses matching a known signature are broadcasting nearby — it does not confirm recording is happening. Bluetooth range and environmental factors affect detection. On iOS, detection uses BLE only; the app reaches a "present" state but not "active" (an Apple platform limitation, not a code gap).

Glasses Radar is built for anyone who wants situational awareness about smart eyewear in their environment.

Andere Apps zeigen dir eine Liste von Bluetooth-Geräten. LensAware sagt dir, welche davon Kamerabrillen sind und wie nah sie sind.
Kamerabrillen sehen aus wie normale Brillen. Sie können ein Tastenfeld am Geldautomaten filmen, ein Klassenzimmer, ein Kind auf dem Spielplatz, ein Gesicht, das jemand später online sucht. Kaum jemand bemerkt sie.

WAS KEIN ANDERER DETEKTOR KANN

Know when smart glasses are advertising near you.

Camera-carrying smart glasses announce themselves over Bluetooth when they power on, pair or come out of their case. Spex listens for those signals and tells you, calmly and plainly, when a matching device is detected nearby.

Spex detects devices such as Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, Meta Ray-Ban Display, Snap Spectacles, RayNeo, Rokid, Looktech, Solos AirGo Vision and Xiaomi AI Glasses when they advertise over Bluetooth. Meta Quest headsets are recognised too, and named as headsets rather than mistaken for glasses.

LIVE RADAR
• Detections appear in real time on the Radar while Spex is open
• Every detection carries a confidence band: Possible, Likely or Confirmed
• Proximity is shown as Immediate, Near or Far, with a closer, further or steady trend, never a made-up distance
• Open a detection to see the model, when it was first and last seen, its signal trend and the technical details behind the match
• Settings › Nearby signals lists every Bluetooth device the scan hears while Spex is open, so you can see exactly what it is working with

ALERTS WHILE YOUR PHONE IS IN YOUR POCKET
• Get a Lock Screen alert when glasses are detected nearby, even with Spex closed
• Confirmed alerts name the device and its range; Likely alerts name the device
• Possible-match alerts tell you when a nearby device partly matches smart glasses; turn them off in Settings if you only want stronger matches
• Alerts are throttled per device, so a busy street doesn't flood your phone

APPLE WATCH
• A discreet tap on your wrist with the device name and proximity
• A complication shows whether Spex is watching and when it last alerted

LOCK SCREEN AND DYNAMIC ISLAND
• While Spex is watching, a quiet Live Activity shows its status and how many devices are nearby, with a Stop button

SHORTCUTS AND ACTION BUTTON
• Start and stop watching with Siri and Shortcuts: Arm Spex, Disarm Spex and Toggle Spex
• Assign Toggle Spex to the Action Button to arm or disarm with one press

HISTORY
• A log of what was detected and when, with its confidence and proximity
• Delete single entries or erase the whole history. No location is recorded.

YOUR CIRCLE
• Add your own glasses, or a friend's, so they stop alerting
• Where the signal allows, an entry covers that one device, so silencing your pair doesn't silence a stranger's of the same model
• Ignore any detection for an hour with one tap

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
• Detection runs entirely on your iPhone
• No accounts and no analytics
• Scan data never leaves your phone: nothing about detections, History or Your Circle is ever sent
• Alert summaries go only to your paired Apple Watch
• Spex listens passively. It never connects to, pairs with or transmits to any device.
• Device support is built into the app, and new models arrive with app updates

WHAT SPEX CAN AND CAN'T SEE
Spex detects Bluetooth advertisements. It does not detect recording or streaming. It catches glasses as they power on, pair or leave their case. Glasses that are already connected and idle broadcast rarely, and no detector can promise otherwise; glasses that aren't advertising can't be seen at all. iOS also limits Bluetooth scanning in the background, so background alerts can be delayed, especially in Low Power Mode, and some devices, including Meta Quest headsets, can only be detected while Spex is open. Detection is best-effort: a quiet Radar is not a guarantee that no smart glasses are nearby.

description:
SpecterSense detects nearby smart glasses by scanning for their Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) advertising signals. When camera-equipped smart glasses from Meta, Snap, or Luxottica are broadcasting nearby, the app alerts you in real time — giving you awareness of potential recording devices in your vicinity.

How It Works
Every BLE device broadcasts small data packets called advertising frames that include a manufacturer identifier assigned by the Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG). These identifiers are standardized, mandatory, and immutable — making them a reliable detection signal. SpecterSense continuously scans for these broadcasts and matches them against known smart glasses manufacturers, including Meta Platforms, Meta Platforms Technologies (Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses), Luxottica Group (Ray-Ban Meta frames), and Snap Inc. (Spectacles).
When a match is detected within your configured range, you receive an immediate push notification and haptic alert — even if the app is running in the background.

Key Features
Real-Time BLE Scanning — Continuously monitors for smart glasses advertising frames using Apple's Core Bluetooth framework.
Proximity Estimation — Uses RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) to estimate whether a detected device is nearby, and displays distance categories from Immediate to Far.
Adjustable Detection Range — Set your own RSSI threshold to control how close a device must be before triggering an alert. Fine-tune sensitivity to your environment.
Push Notifications & Haptic Alerts — Receive immediate, unmissable alerts the moment smart glasses are detected within range.
Background Scanning — Detection continues even when the app is not in the foreground, so you stay informed without actively monitoring.
Detection Log — Every detection event is logged with a timestamp, manufacturer ID, signal strength, and estimated proximity. Export your log for personal records.
Custom Manufacturer IDs — Add any BLE manufacturer company ID (hex value) to scan for additional devices beyond the built-in list.
Zero Data Collection — SpecterSense collects no user data, sends no telemetry, displays no ads, and transmits nothing off your device. All detection data stays local on your iPhone.

Supported Devices
The app monitors for the following Bluetooth SIG Company IDs:

Meta Platforms, Inc.
Meta Platforms Technologies, LLC (Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses)
Luxottica Group S.p.A. (Ray-Ban Meta frames)
Snap Inc. (Spectacles)

You can add additional manufacturer IDs through the Settings tab.

Important Notes
Because detection is based on manufacturer company IDs shared across a manufacturer's entire product line, the app may also alert on other Bluetooth-enabled products from the same companies — such as Meta Quest VR headsets. Context matters: if you receive an alert in a public setting where VR headsets are unlikely, the detection is more likely to correspond to smart glasses.
Detection depends on the target device actively broadcasting BLE advertising frames. Devices in airplane mode, with Bluetooth disabled, or not actively advertising will not be detected. Signal strength can be affected by physical obstacles, body absorption, and device orientation.
This app is a passive awareness tool. It reads publicly broadcast BLE advertising data and does not connect to, interact with, or interfere with any detected devices.

Your Privacy, Your Awareness

Smart glasses with built-in cameras can be difficult to distinguish from ordinary eyewear. SpecterSense gives you an additional layer of situational awareness — a simple, private, on-device tool to help you know when camera-equipped wearables may be nearby.

description:
Know when you're on camera.

Camera glasses look like glasses. Pocket cams clip to shirts. AI pendants record all day. Counterlens listens to the Bluetooth signals capture hardware can't help broadcasting — and maps it around you.

A RADAR, NOT A RUMOR MILL
Every detection is graded — confirmed, probable, or possible — and opens to the raw evidence that produced it: advertised name, manufacturer ID, services, and the exact rule that matched. Audit the radar like an engineer.

SIX CLASSES OF CAPTURE HARDWARE
Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta glasses. Snap Spectacles. Rokid, RayNeo, Xiaomi, Brilliant Labs, even no-name imports. GoPro, DJI Osmo, and Insta360 pocket cams. Plaud and Limitless AI recorder pendants. Plus audio-only and display-only glasses, labeled honestly as lesser risks.

A QUEST IS NOT GLASSES
Other scanners flag sleeping VR headsets as "smart glasses nearby." Counterlens identifies Quest-family hardware and files it as informational — never an alarm.

ACTIVE-CAPTURE FLAG
GoPro-class cameras broadcast state bits. When the encoder-busy flag is set, Counterlens shows "active capture likely" — a live readout no other scanner ships.

LOCATE — HOT / COLD
Geiger-style haptic ticks speed up as you close in and walk you to the broadcasting camera.

60-SECOND ROOM SWEEP
Checking into a rental? Run the guided sweep: walk the corners while Counterlens listens at full sensitivity, then get a clean report card — every device heard, how close, how sure — plus an honest list of what a passive sweep can't rule out. Share it or keep it. Start a sweep straight from the Action Button.

SENTRY MODE
Prop a phone or iPad by the door of a studio, clinic, or gym: big glanceable status, event log, optional chime. Entrances are where camera glasses broadcast most.

HONEST BY DESIGN
No scanner can hear a radio that isn't talking. Glasses broadcast at power-on, pairing, and case-open — and can go quiet while worn and connected. Counterlens tells you exactly when detection works instead of selling false comfort, and every alert is advisory, not an accusation.

PRIVATE TO THE BONE
No account. No analytics. No ads. No location. Zero network calls — there is no server. Your encounter history lives on your iPhone alone, and the full detection database is plain JSON you can inspect in Settings.

Monitor live Bluetooth signal strength.

Receive proximity guidance as signal strength changes.

Use iPhone vibration and audio cues to assist with locating devices.

View last-seen connection information.

One of the app's main features is helping users locate their Meta smart glasses even when the glasses are folded.

As long as the glasses remain powered on and transmit a detectable Bluetooth signal, the app can identify their signal and provide proximity guidance without requiring the glasses to be unfolded.

Camera glasses look like ordinary glasses. What gives them away is the Bluetooth advertisement they broadcast before they connect to anything, and LensAlert is built to read exactly that — then to be straight with you about the rest.

It tells you two things: how well a nearby signal matches a known smart-glasses signature, and roughly how close it seems. Never more than that, and it says so on every screen that could be misread.

WHAT YOU SEE

• Signal field — likely glasses in one colour, every other Bluetooth device in another, each with a rough distance band
• The reason behind the verdict — strong, likely or possible, and what actually matched: a manufacturer ID, a service UUID or an advertised name. The match is shown, not asserted
• Proximity in feet or metres, as bands rather than an invented number
• Sightings history, so a passer-by looks different from something that keeps coming back
• Your Circle — label your own pair and your friends' so familiar frames never raise an alarm
• Device Log — every Bluetooth device this iPhone can hear, with the raw advertisement fields the detector reads. Export it as CSV
• Camera class, stated — display-only and audio-only eyewear is named, not alarmed. Frames without a camera are no reason to look up
• Local alerts, snoozable for an hour or eight, a Home Screen widget, a Control Center toggle, and an Apple Watch companion
• Demo signals, so you can see how detection behaves when nothing is broadcasting nearby

WHY IT SOMETIMES HEARS NOTHING

This part lives in the product, not only in this description. Glasses advertise loudest while powering on, while pairing, and when they leave the case. A pair already connected to its owner's phone can stay quiet for long stretches — and a quiet room reads exactly like an empty one. Background detection is narrower still: iOS limits what any app may listen for while it is off screen.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO

• It cannot tell you whether anything is being recorded. Recording is not broadcast over Bluetooth. A signal means a device is nearby, and nothing about what its owner is doing with it.
• It cannot tell you who is wearing them, and it cannot point a direction. One antenna cannot produce a bearing, so there is no arrow — an arrow would be a guess drawn as a fact.
• Distance is inferred from signal strength alone. Bodies, walls and pockets move it dramatically. Read it as nearer or farther, not as a measurement.

NOTHING LEAVES YOUR PHONE

No account, no ads, no analytics SDK, no location, no network calls to us. Detection runs entirely on this device, and the Device Log stays here unless you export it yourself. The App Privacy section above says Data Not Collected because it is literally true: we run no server that could receive it.

RECOGNISED SIGNATURES

Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta, Snap Spectacles, Even Realities, Brilliant Labs, RayNeo, Vuzix, and a widening set of camera-equipped eyewear — matched on manufacturer IDs, service UUIDs and advertised-name patterns, not a single brand list.

FREE AND PRO

Scanning with the app open is free, permanently, and it is the whole detector: not a trial and not a reduced engine. Pro covers the hours you are not looking at the screen — alerts while the app is closed, the Live Activity, sightings history, labels for glasses you already know, and the widget. Pro does not improve detection. The same engine runs for everyone.

LensAlert Pro is offered as a weekly or a yearly subscription. The price is shown in your local currency before you confirm, and payment is charged to your Apple Account at confirmation of purchase. It renews automatically unless auto-renew is switched off at least 24 hours before the current period ends; manage or cancel in your Apple Account settings.

WHAT IS AIRA?
The Aira Explorer app connects blind and low vision users with on-demand, remote, professional Visual Interpreters who provide access to visual information through your camera view, real-time location, and a specialized dashboard of tools. With one tap, connect and collaborate on tasks involving visual information, from navigating a new space to reading a menu or checking a label. Aira is a trusted, HIPAA-compliant, secure service that enhances independence on your terms.

HIGHLIGHTS
• Connect with a Visual Interpreter 24 hours a day, seven days a week, no reservations required
• Create a free account, then make your first call from the app to unlock 60 free minutes to use throughout your first month
• Enjoy free access at major retailers like Walmart, Starbucks, and Target, over 50 airports, over 50 universities, banks, museums, and more
• Go hands-free with AI glasses from Meta and connect with a Visual Interpreter without holding your phone
• Opt in to Build AI to support the development of Aira AI, our AI-powered Visual Interpreter

HOW DOES AIRA WORK?
Download Aira Explorer, create an account, and connect with a professional Visual Interpreter with one tap. Aira streams live video, including your GPS location, so a Visual Interpreter can see your surroundings through an integrated dashboard. Using your phone's camera, they'll support navigation, description, and narration, guided by your requests and questions. Visual Interpreters can also take and save images to your account, search the web, send messages to you via chat or email, and integrate with your Lyft account. 

Aira is also available on desktop or hands-free with AI glasses from Meta. 

ARE THERE AI FEATURES AVAILABLE?
Access AI is Aira's free image chat feature. Take or upload a photo through the Access AI tab and you'll get an AI-generated description trained by the blind and low vision community. Ask follow-up questions, get a refined answer, or use Aira Verify for a free confirmation of the description by a Visual Interpreter. Popular uses include reading labels, signs, and printed menus, choosing an outfit, and reading a digital display like a thermostat.

HOW CAN I GET AIRA MINUTES?
Access Partners are leading organizations that give their customers, visitors, students, and employees free access to Aira. Call from an Access Partner location and the offer applies automatically, at no cost to you. To browse offers manually, open the app and tap "Browse Access Offers" to see recently used offers or those available near you. Access Partners include over 50 airports and over 50 universities nationwide, plus major retailers like Walmart, Starbucks, and Target in the U.S.

Aira also runs ongoing promotions, including a daily five-minute free call, free minutes for those seeking employment, and support for small business owners.
